read: On 36 solo-wrong cases, the flash-lite holdout adopts the wrong answer 0.2222 under two unanimous wrong peers but only 0.1389 when one of the two instead asserts the CORRECT answer (a single dissenter), a directional reduction of 0.0833. This is CONSISTENT with the classic Asch finding that a single ally breaks conformity (the deference depends on a unanimous board), but it is NOT significant at this sample size (paired McNemar gain=5 lose=2, p=0.453125; only 7 discordant cases): n is capped at the 36 solo-wrong cases in the scanned set. Reported honestly as a suggestive-but-underpowered dissenter effect; a larger solo-wrong pool (or a lower-baseline-accuracy set) would be needed to confirm it.
